references.text: The context of the event where Aaron and Hur support Moses' hands during the battle against Amalek
Aaron and Hur are mentioned again together as leaders appointed to lead the people while Moses was on the mountain
Moses describes himself as 'heavy in mouth' (כְבַד־פֶּה), using the same root כבד as for his heavy hands
A prophetic promise to strengthen weak hands (יָדַיִם רָפוֹת), contrasting with Moses' heavy hands that needed support
The Lord's right hand and arm brought victory, parallel to Moses' raised hands that secured victory
Help comes from the Lord, parallel to the support Moses received to keep his hands lifted toward heaven
The lament notes that it is good to wait quietly for the Lord's salvation, as Moses waited until sunset
The exhortation to strengthen drooping hands, an allusion to the need for support that Moses experienced
Paul urges men to lift holy hands in prayer, parallel to Moses' raised hands in intercession
A parallel about God using stones to ease human weakness and provide rest in a critical situation.
The contrast between Moses' glory (a face that shone) and his weakness (heavy hands), showing the wholeness of his service.
